key_insight: Orchestrated large language models can extract patient pathways and guideline rules directly from unstructured text to perform conformance checking without computer-interpretable guidelines.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make guideline adherence auditing more practical in hospitals where formal machine-readable guidelines are unavailable.
method: Extracted patient traces from discharge letters using LLM-supported components
Identified normative rules from textual stroke guidelines
Translated rules into executable scripts and computed a Trace Conformance Indicator
evidence_signal: In a stroke care evaluation at Alessandria Hospital, hundreds of traces were assessed against 50 guideline-derived rules, and more than 86% of available traces were conformant.
watch_item: Performance may depend on LLM reliability, text quality, and local guideline wording, so results still need careful validation before broader deployment.
paper_title: LLM-Orchestrated Conformance Checking in Stroke Care Without Computer-Interpretable Guidelines
